content_blocks.text: What about the pre-selection thresholds for works and using standard selection? Also, what is the situation with regards PAS91 and CAS?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What about the pre-selection thresholds for works and using standard selection? Also, what is the situation with regards PAS91 and CAS?

content_blocks.text: The Act takes the same approach to defining below threshold works contracts as currently in the PCR 2015: ie, for these purposes only, the works threshold is taken to be equal to the appropriate supplies/services threshold for that authority. As with the standard CCS SQ, we await guidance to confirm how PAS91 and CAS will operate under the Act.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.

content_blocks.text: Section 22 of the Act states that the criteria may assess legal/financial capacity OR technical ability. Could this also be AND, ie, you could include criteria to assess both?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Section 22 of the Act states that the criteria may assess legal/financial capacity OR technical ability. Could this also be AND, ie, you could include criteria to assess both?

content_blocks.text: This is an interesting point. On the face of it, the drafting could be read to require a choice between one or the other, although this would be a departure from the position under the PCR 2015 where economic/financial standing AND technical/professional ability may be assessed.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Section 22 of the Act states that the criteria may assess legal/financial capacity OR technical ability. Could this also be AND, ie, you could include criteria to assess both?

content_blocks.text: Section 22 does state that conditions of participation may only be used if doing so is proportionate to do so having regard to the nature and complexity of the contract; whether to use both will need to be proportionate accordingly.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Section 22 of the Act states that the criteria may assess legal/financial capacity OR technical ability. Could this also be AND, ie, you could include criteria to assess both?

content_blocks.text: Can you still require suppliers to have delivered a comparable contract as a condition of participation (albeit not requiring them to have worked with a particular authority)?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Can you still require suppliers to have delivered a comparable contract as a condition of participation (albeit not requiring them to have worked with a particular authority)?

content_blocks.text: Yes, this should be possible subject to the general requirement that any condition of participation must be proportionate having regard to the nature and complexity of the contract.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Can you still require suppliers to have delivered a comparable contract as a condition of participation (albeit not requiring them to have worked with a particular authority)?

content_blocks.text: A requirement to have delivered a contract like the one being procured, in terms of value/scope, seems likely to be proportionate.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Can you still require suppliers to have delivered a comparable contract as a condition of participation (albeit not requiring them to have worked with a particular authority)?

content_blocks.text: Any condition of participation will need to respect the rules on specifications and equivalents (for example, it would not be lawful to require a supplier to have previously supplied a particular brand of product where alternative products are available that meet the requirements).
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Can you still require suppliers to have delivered a comparable contract as a condition of participation (albeit not requiring them to have worked with a particular authority)?

content_blocks.text: Does the new contract subject matter need to be the same or closely related to the bad performance/contract performance notice if considering exclusion?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Does the new contract subject matter need to be the same or closely related to the bad performance/contract performance notice if considering exclusion?

content_blocks.text: This is a very interesting question. At present there is nothing in the Act that suggests that the subject matter of the previously poorly performed contract must be related to that which is currently being procured. Schedule 7(12) simply refers to a “relevant contract”, which in turn is defined as one to which a contracting authority or other public body (whether in the UK or outside of it) is a party. There is no requirement in the definition of “relevant contract” for the subject matter to be related.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Does the new contract subject matter need to be the same or closely related to the bad performance/contract performance notice if considering exclusion?

content_blocks.text: That said, given that suppliers will tend to work in certain sectors and offer particular types of goods/services/works, there is very likely to be a link between the subject matters of the two contracts in question, given that the supplier is the same.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Does the new contract subject matter need to be the same or closely related to the bad performance/contract performance notice if considering exclusion?

content_blocks.text: What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: There is no stated process for challenging an authority issuing a contract performance notice – beyond that which is generally available to suppliers under the Act for breach of the Act.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: If a contract performance notice is inaccurate, then potentially a supplier could bring a claim under the Act against the publishing authority for breach of the duty to publish a compliant contract performance notice and more generally for breach of section 12 duties around transparency, proportionality, and equal treatment.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: The usual 30-day limitation period for a procurement claim would apply and would be likely to start to run from the publication date of the Contract Performance Notice. Such a claim might well be brought alongside a general contract law claim disputing termination for the breach in question.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: A supplier who was excluded from a procurement based on a defective contract performance notice would be required to inform the contracting authority in the current procurement of the defect.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: This might well give rise to a duty on that contracting authority to uphold its section 12 duties to act transparently, proportionately, and afford equal treatment, by looking into the detail of the contract performance notice and the supplier’s complaint around it.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: Of course, a supplier must always be given an opportunity to make representations and demonstrate self-cleaning prior to any exclusion. However, as set out above, where a supplier did not make a timely challenge to the publication of the Contract Performance Notice within 30 days of its publication, it will almost certainly have lost the right to do so now, due to the limitation period. It is possible that this is an area where guidance may be issued from the Procurement Review Unit.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
What is the process for challenging the issue of a contract performance notice? What liability or risks are there to a contracting authority for issuing a contract performance notice if challenged?

content_blocks.text: Are the changes under the Act likely to increase or decrease the number of contract terminations/exclusions?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Are the changes under the Act likely to increase or decrease the number of contract terminations/exclusions?

content_blocks.text: This remains to be seen, but it seems likely that the need to refer all exclusions on to the relevant debarment authority for consideration for investigation may make authorities more cautious about exclusions and reserve these for the most clear-cut cases.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Are the changes under the Act likely to increase or decrease the number of contract terminations/exclusions?

content_blocks.text: What will happen if a supplier is investigated and the relevant debarment authority decides they do not need to be added to the debarment list? Does that undermine the decision made by the contracting authority? Could a supplier challenge based on this?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs

What will happen if a supplier is investigated and the relevant debarment authority decides they do not need to be added to the debarment list? Does that undermine the decision made by the contracting authority? Could a supplier challenge based on this?

content_blocks.text: This will depend on the reason why the supplier is not added to the debarment list at the end of the investigation. It is possible that the debarment authority may agree with the exclusion but still decide not to exclude. More information is needed on the remit and powers of the relevant debarment authority to answer this question. It seems highly unlikely that it will have the power to “overturn” an exclusion decision made by a contracting authority as this is the prerogative of court via a formal claim.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs

What will happen if a supplier is investigated and the relevant debarment authority decides they do not need to be added to the debarment list? Does that undermine the decision made by the contracting authority? Could a supplier challenge based on this?

content_blocks.text: Will the risk of a supplier being added to the debarment list incentivise that supplier to potentially challenge the decision to exclude them, to mitigate them becoming debarred?
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
FAQs
Will the risk of a supplier being added to the debarment list incentivise that supplier to potentially challenge the decision to exclude them, to mitigate them becoming debarred?

content_blocks.text: Yes, our understanding is that the debarment list will be a publicly available document. It is not yet clear how much direct involvement ministers will have with individual debarment decisions, but it certainly seems likely where the exclusion is for a high profile offence that is politically relevant or sensitive.
heading_path: The selection stage under the Act.
